Article Title: After Rahul Gandhi, Union home minister Amit Shah raises concern over rampant drug abuse in Punjab

BATHINDA: After Rahul Gandhi, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, union home minister Amit Shah has raised concerns over the rampant drug abuse in Punjab. Citing two incidents in less than one half month wherein one anti-drug activist was shot dead and a father if a drug addict youth had to commit suicide, the union minister has stated that the home ministry will seek response from Punjab government over both the incidents.HM made the observations on Friday, a day after Rahul Gandhi had raised concern over drug abuse in the state.HM Amit Shah in a oust in X on Friday wrote thatPunjab is grappling with the rising threats of drugs, gangsterism, and organized crime. The biggest question before the Bhagwant Mann government is who will ultimately take responsibility for the safety of Punjab's people?In Dirba, a father taking poison under pressure, and in Mansa, the broad-daylight murder of Parvinder Singh Jhotta—who had raised his voice against drugs—have raised serious questions about law and order in Punjab. Parvinder's father has leveled grave allegations against the AAP government and their MLA. The Home Ministry will also seek responses from the Punjab government on both these incidents.In Punjab, the drug trade is flourishing, the threat of organized crime is growing, and questions are being raised about the safety of those who speak out against drugs.Bhagwant Mann, the people of Punjab do not want publicity—they want answers; not announcements, but results; decisive strikes against drug networks, and an impartial investigation into any political patronage provided to criminals.He further wrote Today, I reiterate my pledge before the people of Punjab that when our government comes to power in Punjab, we will work with full force to create a drug-free, gangster-free, and secure Punjab. Our goal is clear—strikes against the drug trade, protection of our youth's future, strict action against criminals, and the rule of law in such a way that no citizen is forced to live under the shadow of fear.
Article Summary: HM made the observations on Friday, a day after Rahul Gandhi had raised concern over drug abuse in the state. The biggest question before the Bhagwant Mann government is who will ultimately take responsibility for the safety of Punjab's people, he wrote.

Article Title: 'Bangladesh-style regime change' bid: Rajnath slams opposition over Delhi protests
Article Text:
'Conspiracy to seize power by anarchy': Rajnath Singh slams Congress protest against EC, says party seeks 'regime change'

Rajnath Singh targets Rahul Gandhi

BJP alleges conspiracy to destabilise country

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Friday accused the Congress and its allies of attempting to destabilise India through protests against the Election Commission , alleging that their objective was to bring about a Bangladesh-style regime change by creating political unrest.Addressing a press conference in Lucknow, Singh said opposition parties were using young people as instruments of political confrontation and attempting to create chaos under the pretext of electoral reforms and the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise."Attempts are being made to use the nation's youth as pawns in a politics of chaos. Some seek a regime change—modelled after the events in Bangladesh—openly admitting that they drew inspiration from the situation in Bangladesh; others, meanwhile, brazenly call for the toppling of the government. This makes it clear that their sole agenda is to dismantle democratic institutions and set the country ablaze...their struggle is not for electoral reform, nor is it about SIR or Gyanesh Kumar; it is not for the sake of a bright future for the nation's youth—rather, it is a conspiracy to seize power by inciting anarchy in the country. .."The defence minister's remarks come amid continuing protests by opposition parties, INDIA bloc leaders and student organisations against the Election Commission's electoral roll revision exercise and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Singh also targeted Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, accusing him of undermining constitutional institutions and using allegations of electoral irregularities for political gains."India's constitutional bodies cannot be made sacrificial for political interests. This needs to be understood. Through false outrage, attempts to malign institutions and political opportunism, India's development journey cannot be affected. Instead of indulging in politics of disruption, Rahul Gandhi should respect the public mandate and do self-introspection of his political role."The defence minister further questioned Gandhi's allegations concerning voter lists, citing claims involving alleged duplicate and fake voters."Rahul Gandhi once claimed that a 70-year-old woman was a double voter. On another occasion, he alleged that a 35-year-old woman was a 124-year-old voter. At times, he even attempted to defame ordinary citizens by labelling them as fake voters...his own party never filed a single formal appeal regarding the electoral rolls; the reason being that they had absolutely no evidence to support such claims. We have never cast doubt upon constitutional institutions—that is simply our character. We have never questioned the nation’s electoral system, nor have we ever sought to mislead the public by defaming constitutional institutions. We have always held the people of this country, the Constitution, and our constitutional institutions in high regard..."Singh maintained that the Congress had failed to substantiate its allegations against the electoral system and accused the opposition of attempting to discredit constitutional institutions.Uttar Pradesh BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary also alleged that efforts were underway to destabilise the country and interfere with constitutional institutions."A conspiracy to destabilise the country is going on. An attempt to make changes to constitutional bodies is also being made..."Rajnath also took a swipe at the Congress's electoral prospects in Uttar Pradesh, pointing to its prolonged absence from power in the state and questioning Rahul Gandhi's political strength without the support of the Samajwadi Party."The Congress party has been out of power in Uttar Pradesh for 37 years...I would like to ask Rahul Gandhi: without the Samajwadi Party, do you even have the capability to win your own seat in Rae Bareli?"
Article Summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh accuses Congress of attempting to destabilise India through protests against the Election Commission. Singh says opposition parties are using young people as instruments of political confrontation and attempting to create chaos under the pretext of electoral reforms. Singh also targeted Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, accusing him of undermining constitutional institutions.

American singer Mary Millben has alleged that billionaire George Soros is funding protests in India, reiterating her support for Prime Minister Narendra Modi and targeting Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke.In a video message, Millben claimed that Soros and people associated with him were financing protests against conservative leaders across the world, urging young Indians to rally behind Modi and counter what she described as “chaos and destruction”.“The name is George Soros and that whole machine of people are constantly funding a lot of these protests and chaos that's breaking out across the world,” she said.The remarks follow Millben's October 14 post on X, in which she alleged that Dipke and the CJP were receiving funding from US-based donors opposed to Modi. She had also called on young Indians to organise a peaceful counter-movement against the protests, framing them as an attempt to create disruption in the country.Abhijeet Dipke had hit back at Millben on X, questioning the involvement of foreign nationals in India's domestic affairs.‘We don't need outsiders interfering in our country's affairs,’ he said.Mary Millben further criticised Rahul Gandhi and Dipke, accusing them of creating disruption without offering solutions.Comparing the protests with movements in the United States, she cited the civil rights movement led by Martin Luther King Jr. as an example of peaceful mobilisation that brought legislative change.“Your voice should want to bring about change that unifies the country and that works with everyone to find the best solution for the people that you serve,” she said.Millben also urged Dipke to engage directly with the government rather than continue the protests, saying he should use his ability to mobilise people constructively. Article Title: Middle East conflict: India pushes for 'resolution through dialogue and diplomacy' at UNSC
Article Text:
Harish said India had “very high stakes” in the safety, security and stability of the region

India flags attacks on commercial ships

Calls for de-escalation, protection of maritime routes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Parvathaneni Harish, on Friday condemned attacks on commercial vessels and civilian infrastructure in the Middle East, warning that the escalating hostilities pose a serious threat to regional stability and the safety of Indian nationals.Speaking at the UN Security Council ’s open debate on the Middle East, Harish said India had “very high stakes” in the safety, security and stability of the region, highlighting that around 10 million Indians live in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries and contribute to their economies.He called for restraint and de-escalation, expressing concern over attacks on civilian infrastructure that have resulted in casualties, including the death of Indian citizen Mohammed Yusuf Ali in Riyadh.Harish said India stood in complete solidarity with the government and people of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty following the recent attacks.He also raised concerns over attacks on commercial shipping, including the India-flagged MV DP World Kaveri earlier this week and MT Petro Dolphin and MT Walthera last week.“All attacks on commercial shipping and merchant mariners are legally and morally indefensible,” he said, adding that several of the affected vessels had Indian seafarers whose safety and security remained India's direct responsibility.India reiterated the need for an immediate de-escalation of hostilities and a resolution to the conflict through dialogue and diplomacy.Harish said attacks on commercial vessels, seafarers and civilian infrastructure must cease, stressing that freedom of navigation and the safe, unimpeded flow of maritime commerce through international waterways must be upheld in accordance with international law.He further added that focus on maritime security must not divert attention from the humanitarian crisis in Gaza. It condemned the October 7, 2023 attacks and reiterated its support for a negotiated two-state solution, the full implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 2803, and continued development and humanitarian assistance.v
Article Summary: India’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Parvathaneni Harish, on Friday condemned attacks on commercial vessels and civilian infrastructure in the Middle East. Harish said India had “very high stakes” in the safety, security and stability of the region.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday said it will be problematic if every citizen becomes a journalist as PILs sought protection of the right to freedom of expression of freelancers, independent journalists and reel-makers who descend in large numbers at protest venues already teeming with hordes of accredited reporters from registered media houses.Senior advocate Indira Jaising complained to a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi that Delhi Police did not recognise independent and freelance journalists covering the protests and insisted on Press Information Bureau (PIB) accreditation. She said there must be a national protocol for police not to obstruct the professional work of any journalist who has an identity card from the employer.CJI Kant, however, struck a note of caution. “We must also keep one thing in mind. If everyone starts becoming a journalist, it will create problems for every other person,” he said. Justice Bagchi said, “It will require a detailed examination whether the right to freedom of expression will empower every citizen of this country to be a journalist. That is difficult. There are layers of protection for accredited journalists, those employed in registered media houses or whether they are freelance journalists, influencers or reel-makers.CJI Kant said, “The issue requires detailed examination — whether there should be a certain category of journalists to whom extra level of protection should be given.” Justice Bagchi added, “The Working Journalists Act makes classes among journalists. We must examine all that.”Solicitor general Tushar Mehta said in the present era of digital technology, any person with a mobile phone could claim to be an independent or freelance journalist when he/she would, in fact, be only making reels to garner popularity on social media to earn money by either presenting one-sided stories or sensationalising incidents.Mehta supported the contention that women journalists should not be harrassed, but argued that the same consideration should be extended to women police personnel as well.
Article Summary: PILs sought protection of the right to freedom of expression of freelancers, independent journalists and reel-makers who descend in large numbers at protest venues. Senior advocate Indira Jaising complained to a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi that Delhi Police did not recognise independent and freelance journalists.

Article Title: Violent Naxalism isover, task now is toheal wounds: Amit Shah
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Home minister Amit Shah Thursday said not just Left-wing extremism but every trace of misery caused by five decades of Maoist violence must be wiped out. At an event in Chhattisgarh to distribute assistive devices to victims maimed in Naxal attacks, he accused Congress of failing to provide basic amenities for decades.Addressing the event via video conferencing, Shah said the programme, organised under 'seva sankalp abhiyan' to mark 25 years of PM Modi's 'seva and samarpan' (service), would help tribal people who had lost limbs or sensory abilities due to Naxal violence. Chhattisgarh govt organised it with welfare organisations such as Bhagwan Mahaveer Viklang Sahayata Samiti and Bharatiya Jain Sanghatana to provide prosthetic devices, wheelchairs, crutches and hearing aids.Held in Jagdalpur from Oct 5 to 7, the campaign benefited over 3,600 persons with disabilities, including over 1,570 from Bastar. Shah said Maoists' use of IEDs to maim innocent civilians for political objectives was a grave human rights violation.Though violent Naxalism was eliminated by the March 31, 2026 deadline, Shah said, the task would remain unfinished until govt healed victims' wounds, helped them stand and ensured they lived with dignity.Bastar was becoming vibrant again, he said, citing participation in Bastar Olympics and Bastar Pandum. Shah said 8,526 Naxalites had surrendered. Accounts had been opened for 7,328, reward money given to 1,620, incentives provided to 7,882, jobs offered to 455 and land allotted to 129. Another 4,014 beneficiaries had received houses under PM Awas Yojana, while over 2,308 tribal people had undergone skill training.A total of 6,763 ration cards had been issued, 2,808 families provided free electricity and work begun on 372 road projects. 48,526 people had received Aadhaar cards and 44 gram panchayats were recognised under 'Ilwad Panchayat Awards'.Twenty of the 50 security camps in Chhattisgarh will be converted into Shaheed Veer Gundadhur Seva Dera, providing public services, skill training and PDS benefits to nearby villages, Shah said. "The places where our security forces once sat to protect you will become the places where officials will lay the foundation for a developed Bastar," Shah added. tnn
Article Summary: Home minister Amit Shah said every trace of misery caused by five decades of Maoist violence must be wiped out. At an event in Chhattisgarh to distribute assistive devices to victims maimed in Naxal attacks, he accused Congress of failing to provide basic amenities for decades.

Article Title: 'Ready to be detained': Dipke defiant ahead of Tiranga march in Delhi
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Thursday claimed police personnel were keeping him under surveillance and said he could be detained overnight or on Friday morning, ahead of the outfit’s planned national flag-waving protest at Connaught Place.Addressing a press conference late Thursday, Dipke said he was prepared to go to jail for waving the Tricolour as the CJP called on supporters to gather at Central Park on Friday, despite the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) announcing a two-day closure of the venue.“Tomorrow, we will peacefully go and wave the Tiranga. As the citizens of this country, if you consider this to be a crime, then you are the biggest traitor,” Dipke said, as quoted by news agency PTI.“If we have to go to jail to wave the Tiranga in this country, then we are ready for it,” he added.Dipke questioned the decision to shut the park, saying the authorities could not close every location where the outfit might organise a demonstration. “Tomorrow, we will say that we will wave the Tiranga at 100 places. So you will shut down all 100 places?” he said.On X, Dipke alleged that undercover police personnel had surrounded his accommodation and were following him in a white Scorpio.The proposed march is part of the CJP’s campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The outfit has demanded Kumar’s resignation, alleging that more than 13 crore voters were deleted.Delhi Police has urged people to stay away from the gathering, citing prohibitory orders and saying Connaught Place is not a designated protest site. However, it said a limited group could be allowed to wave the national flag and sing the national anthem at a suitable location.The planned demonstration comes days after CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were sent to judicial custody for entering Jantar Mantar and raising slogans demanding Kumar’s resignation.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke claims police personnel are keeping him under surveillance. Dipke said he could be detained overnight or on Friday morning, ahead of the outfit’s planned national flag-waving protest at Connaught Place.

Article Title: Delhi Police signals conditional nod for flag-waving, anthem at CJP's Oct 16 march amid curbs

NEW DELHI: Ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) proposed ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march at Connaught Place on Friday, Delhi Police said it may consider allowing a select group of people to gather at a suitable location to carry the national flag and sing the national anthem. The statement comes amid restrictions on gatherings in the area and the New Delhi Municipal Council’s (NDMC) decision to shut Central Park for two days.DCP PRO Neha Yadav said the CJP had appealed to the public through social media and a press conference to assemble at Central Park at 5 pm on October 16. She added that the Aam Aadmi Party had also urged its workers, supporters and the general public to attend in large numbers.“Given the current security and law-and-order situation, a prohibitory order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) is already in effect in Connaught Place and its surrounding areas, aimed at maintaining peace and order and ensuring the safety of individuals as well as public and private property,” Yadav said.She said Delhi Police had been asked to make security arrangements at Central Park and prevent unauthorised entry.Yadav also said market and trade associations had sought protection for their establishments, alleging that unlawful gatherings were affecting business during the festive season.“The Delhi Police appeals to protesters and the general public not to participate in any gathering that violates the orders issued under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which is currently in force. Appropriate legal action will be taken against those who violate these orders,” she said.Yadav added that any permitted gathering must follow the prescribed rules for the national flag and anthem. “When carrying or accompanying the national flag, and during the singing of the national anthem, prescribed rules must be followed, and the utmost respect, dignity, and decorum must be maintained toward both the tricolour and the national anthem,” she said.Earlier, in a notice dated October 15, the NDMC said, “It is hereby informed that the Central Park, Connaught Place, shall remain closed to the general public on 16th October 2026 & 17th October 2026, due to administrative reasons.”The closure comes after the CJP announced the march on Wednesday. On Thursday, founder Abhijit Dipke urged political parties and civil society groups to join the protest, saying, “I request all political parties and civil society groups to rise above ideology and come together. If the right to vote is not saved, democracy will not be saved.”Earlier, the Delhi Police told the high court that it will take “appropriate steps” against Dipke’s proposed protest.Police also cited prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), imposed to maintain law and order and protect public and private property.The submission came as the high court heard a plea by Palika Bazar vendor Anil Kumar Gupta, who sought intervention against the proposed ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march, arguing that protests could disrupt business and threaten traders’ livelihoods.The plea was mentioned before acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre on Thursday. Senior advocate Sacchin Puri, appearing for the petitioner, told the court, “This protest has to be stopped.”The march follows the arrest of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who were sent to five days of judicial custody after raising slogans demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation at Jantar Mantar.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) proposed ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march at Connaught Place on Friday. Delhi Police may allow small gathering to wave tricolour, sing anthem at CJP march.NDMC shuts Central Park on October 16-17 for 'administrative reasons'

NEW DELHI: A 30-foot-tall cockroach effigy will be burnt alongside those of Ravan, Kumbhkaran and Meghnad during Dussehra celebrations in the national capital this year, with organisers saying the insect will symbolise filth and unhygienic conditions as part of their cleanliness message.The Shri Keshav Ramlila Committee, which organises the Ramlila in Pitampura, said the initiative aims to highlight the need to eliminate filth from homes, neighbourhoods and society at large, in keeping with the Swachh Bharat and Swachh Delhi campaigns.Ashok Goel Devaraha, president of the committee and Model Town BJP MLA, said the decision was intended to reinforce the message of the triumph of good over evil and was not politically motivated.Speaking to ANI, Devaraha said Vijayadashami symbolises the victory of truth over falsehood and righteousness over unrighteousness. He added that the committee had previously burnt effigies representing issues affecting the country, including Naxalism and terrorism.“Keeping these principles in mind, we have also, in the past, burned effigies representing various afflictions plaguing our nation, such as Naxalism or terrorism.This year, our committee has decided to burn an effigy of a cockroach, a symbol of filth,” he said.The effigy will be set alight at the committee grounds in Pitampura. Devaraha described it as a 30-foot-tall structure shaped like a cockroach, adding that the aim was to draw attention to the need to rid homes, neighbourhoods and society of dirt and unhygienic conditions.The choice of the insect comes amid protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and opposition parties in Delhi, which had been campaigning against former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and is now demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The group staged protests against Pradhan in June and July, including a demonstration at Jantar Mantar and a march towards Parliament on July 20. Pradhan subsequently resigned as education minister in July, while Pralhad Joshi took over the portfolio.The CJP has since returned to the streets over its allegations concerning the electoral roll revision process, joining opposition parties and student organisations in demonstrations. Several activists, students and journalists were detained during protests in the capital.The committee president, however, has denied that the cockroach effigy is politically motivated, maintaining that it is intended to convey a message about cleanliness.Also read: 6,000 cops, 200 CAPF companies: As CJP pushes ahead with Tiranga march, Delhi prepares for a high-security friday On May 15, while hearing a case in the Supreme Court, CJI Surya Kant had compared certain individuals with fraudulent degrees to “cockroaches” who become social media or RTI activists to attack the system. The remarks triggered widespread backlash among young people and inspired the satirical “Cockroach Janta Party” (CJP) movement.He later clarified that his oral remarks during a Supreme Court hearing were “misquoted” and later used with “malicious intent” to mislead the country’s youth.
Article Summary: 30-foot-tall cockroach effigy will be burnt alongside those of Ravan, Kumbhkaran and Meghnad during Dussehra celebrations. Organisers say insect will symbolise filth and unhygienic conditions as part of cleanliness message.

Now, in media and social media, things are going on that govt has apologised and they want to say nothing,” he complained.CJI Kant said, “We have not read those media reports, nor are we taking cognisance of any such report.” Justice Bagchi added, “We are neither taking cognisance of the media reports nor your unqualified apology. He cited Article 74(1) of the Constitution, saying the President could ask the government to reconsider its advice.“I request you to ask the Government to reconsider this appointment, and that Mr. Gautam not take office until the CBI has completed its investigation,” he wrote.Rahul also referred to the family’s continuing demand for justice, saying, “Ankita refused the repellent demand made of her and paid with her life. Union minister HD Kumaraswamy on Thursday accused the Karnataka government of targeting Janata Dal (Secular) workers in connection with an alleged sting operation involving political leaders and officials. Go ahead. Start with me. You can look into my party workers later,” Kumaraswamy said.Alleging that sting operations were being used to blackmail politicians and government officials and extort money, he demanded a wider probe into whether individuals holding positions in constitutional institutions were also being targeted.“All of this must come to light, and that can happen only through a fair investigation,” he said.After ending his sit-in protest, Kumaraswamy said he was giving the state government two days to take action, citing an assurance from police commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh.Kumaraswamy further alleged that a key individual involved in the matter had misused the name of a media organisation and engaged in illegal activities, thereby damaging its reputation.He claimed that the person behind the alleged sting operation targeting Siddaramaiah was close to senior Congress leaders and accused the government of attempting to protect the individual.The minister also alleged that efforts were being made to damage his reputation through the same person.“Against this backdrop, I am giving this government another two days to act,” Kumaraswamy said.The allegations come amid an ongoing police inquiry into the alleged derogatory content involving Siddaramaiah. A powerful magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck the Kamchatka Peninsula region of Russia on Friday, the European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC) said, citing seismic data.According to preliminary information shared by EMSC, the earthquake occurred at a depth of 140 km (87 miles), with its epicentre located around 123 km southwest of Vilyuchinsk in Russia’s Far East. The seismic event was recorded at around 3:35 pm local time.The Kamchatka Peninsula, located along the Pacific coast of Russia, is part of the seismically active Pacific Ring of Fire, where tectonic plate movements frequently trigger earthquakes and volcanic activity.The US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) said there was no tsunami warning, advisory, watch or threat following the earthquake.Further details about the impact of the earthquake, including any reports of damage or casualties, were not immediately available.
Article Summary: Magnitude 7.0 earthquake strikes the Kamchatka Peninsula region of Russia on Friday. Quake occurred at a depth of 140 km (87 miles), with epicentre 123 km southwest of Vilyuchinsk. No tsunami warning, advisory, watch or threat following the earthquake.
